domain_entities.name: LeaveRequest
domain_entities.purpose: Represents an employee's leave application. Tracks the full lifecycle from draft through submission, approval/rejection, and cancellation. Carries the audit trail of who acted and when at each state transition.

domain_entities.name: LeavePolicy
domain_entities.purpose: Defines the rules and entitlements for a specific leave type. Governs how many days are granted, whether accrual applies, notice periods, and whether manager approval is required. Referenced by LeaveBalance and LeaveRequest to enforce business rules.

domain_entities.name: Employee
domain_entities.purpose: Represents an employee in the organization. The employee is the actor who applies for leave and whose leave balances are tracked. The managerId links to the approving manager. Employment status gates whether leave actions are permitted.

domain_entities.name: LeaveBalance
domain_entities.purpose: Tracks an employee's leave entitlement, usage, and remaining balance for a specific leave policy within a fiscal year. Deducted on approval, restored on cancellation of approved leave. Enforces the "cannot apply if insufficient balance" rule.

domain_entities.name: LeaveType
domain_entities.purpose: Enumeration of leave categories. Each type maps to a LeavePolicy that defines its rules. The feature scope covers ANNUAL, SICK, and EMERGENCY; the remaining types are defined for completeness.

domain_entities.name: LeaveRequestStatus
domain_entities.purpose: Enumeration of states a LeaveRequest can occupy. Drives the lifecycle state machine and determines which transitions are legal.

domain_entities.name: EmploymentStatus
domain_entities.purpose: Enumeration of employee employment states. Only ACTIVE employees may apply for leave. INACTIVE and TERMINATED employees are blocked from leave operations.

domain_entities.name: BalanceStatus
domain_entities.purpose: Enumeration of LeaveBalance states. ACTIVE means the balance can be used. EXHAUSTED means remainingDays is 0 and no further leave of this type can be taken. FROZEN means the balance is locked due to employee termination/deactivation.

domain_entities.name: AuditLog
domain_entities.purpose: Immutable record of every state-changing operation across all modules. Satisfies GP-002 (audit trail). Written by AuditService and never updated.

domain_entities.name: Notification
domain_entities.purpose: Stores notifications sent to employees (e.g., leave status changes). Supports delivery tracking and read status.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 1 — Foundation: Audit + Shared Validation
recommended_phases.rationale: Audit is a leaf dependency for every other module (GP-002). Shared validation has no module dependencies. Both must exist before any state-changing module can be built.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 2 — Employee + Policy modules
recommended_phases.rationale: Employee and Policy are the next leaf modules. They depend only on Audit (already built). Leave and Balance both depend on them, so they must come first.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 3 — Balance module
recommended_phases.rationale: Balance depends on Employee, Policy, and Audit (all built). Leave depends on Balance for deductBalance/restoreBalance during approval/rejection flows.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 4 — Notification module
recommended_phases.rationale: Notification depends only on Audit. Leave depends on it for sending status-change notifications. Can be built in parallel with Phase 3 but listed separately for context-window safety.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 5 — Leave module (core)
recommended_phases.rationale: Leave is the orchestrating module. All its dependencies (Employee, Policy, Balance, Audit, Notification, shared/validation) are now in place. This phase builds the LeaveService, LeaveRepository, controller, and routes.

architecture_md_update:
## Leave Management Module

### Overview
The Leave Management module enables employees to apply for annual, sick, and emergency leave, managers to approve or reject requests, and the system to track leave balances. It is built as a set of modules within the modular monolith, following the established layered architecture (presentation → application → domain → infrastructure).

### Domain Entities
- **LeaveRequest** — Core aggregate representing a leave application. Lifecycle: DRAFT → SUBMITTED → APPROVED/REJECTED/CANCELLED. Carries full audit trail (who acted, when).
- **LeavePolicy** — Defines rules per leave type (entitlement, accrual, notice, approval requirement). Lifecycle: ACTIVE ↔ INACTIVE.
- **Employee** — The actor who applies for leave. Employment status (ACTIVE/INACTIVE/TERMINATED) gates eligibility.
- **LeaveBalance** — Tracks entitlement, used, and remaining days per employee per policy per fiscal year. Lifecycle: ACTIVE → EXHAUSTED/FROZEN and back.
- **AuditLog** — Immutable record of every state change (GP-002).
- **Notification** — Stores messages sent to employees (e.g., status changes).
- **Enums**: LeaveType, LeaveRequestStatus, EmploymentStatus, BalanceStatus.

### Business Rules
- **BR-001** — Only ACTIVE employees may create/submit leave requests.
- **BR-002** — Before submission, remaining balance must cover the requested days (endDate - startDate + 1).
- **BR-003** — On approval, balance is deducted; if remaining reaches 0, balance becomes EXHAUSTED. On cancellation of an approved request, balance is restored.

### Database Tables (Conceptual)
All tables use snake_case naming. Primary keys are UUIDs. Foreign keys reference the appropriate parent tables.
- **employees** — Core employee data; indexes on employee_number, email, manager_id, employment_status.
- **leave_policies** — Policy definitions; indexes on leave_type, is_active.
- **leave_requests** — Leave applications with full lifecycle fields (approved_by, rejected_by, cancelled_by, etc.); indexes on employee_id, status, leave_policy_id, start_date, end_date, approved_by.
- **leave_balances** — Per-employee per-policy per-year balances; unique constraint on (employee_id, leave_policy_id, fiscal_year).
- **audit_logs** — Immutable audit trail; indexes on (entity_type, entity_id), performed_by, performed_at, action.
- **notifications** — User notifications; indexes on recipient_id, status, (related_entity_type, related_entity_id), created_at.

### Module Structure
```
src/
├── modules/
│   ├── audit/          # AuditLog model, IAuditRepository, AuditService
│   ├── employee/       # Employee model, IEmployeeRepository, EmployeeService
│   ├── policy/         # LeavePolicy model, IPolicyRepository, PolicyService
│   ├── balance/        # Balance model, IBalanceRepository, BalanceService
│   ├── notification/   # Notification model, INotificationRepository, NotificationService
│   └── leave/          # LeaveRequest model, ILeaveRepository, LeaveService, LeaveController, routes
└── shared/
    └── validation/     # validateLeaveRequest, validateDateRange
```

### Dependencies
- **leave** depends on employee, policy, balance, audit, notification, shared/validation.
- **balance** depends on employee, policy, audit.
- **employee**, **policy**, **notification** each depend on audit.
- No circular dependencies; all flows inward.

### Golden Principles Compliance
- **GP-002 (Audit)**: Every state-changing operation in LeaveService calls `IAuditService.log`. The audit module is a leaf dependency built first.
- **GP-003 (Validation)**: All API inputs are validated at the boundary using shared/validation helpers before reaching services.
- **GP-005 (RBAC)**: Manager-only endpoints (approve, reject, getLeaveRequestsForManager) enforce role checks at the route level before delegating to the service.
- **Transaction semantics**: Balance deduction and restoration are performed atomically within the same database transaction as the leave status update.

### Implementation Phases
1. **Foundation** — Audit + Shared Validation (no module dependencies).
2. **Employee + Policy** — Leaf modules depending only on Audit.
3. **Balance** — Depends on Employee, Policy, Audit.
4. **Notification** — Depends on Audit; can run parallel to Phase 3.
5. **Leave (core)** — Orchestrator; all dependencies ready.

### Integration with Existing System
This module extends the modular monolith without altering existing boundaries. It reuses the shared database connection (`src/shared/db/connection.ts`), follows the same repository pattern (interface + Pg* implementation), and exposes REST endpoints via Fastify routes. The frontend (React Native) consumes these endpoints through the API layer.
sql_schemas: table employees | fields: id, employee_number, first_name, last_name, email, manager_id, department, hire_date, termination_date, employment_status, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at | pk: id | fks: manager_id -> employees.id | indexes: employee_number: unique lookup by employee number; email: unique lookup by email; manager_id: team hierarchy queries — list direct reports for manager approval workflows; employment_status: filter active/inactive/terminated employees for leave eligibility checks

table leave_policies | fields: id, policy_name, leave_type, entitlement_days, accrual_rate, max_accumulation, minimum_notice_days, requires_manager_approval, is_active, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | indexes: leave_type: filter policies by leave type (annual, sick, emergency) when resolving applicable policy for a request; is_active: exclude inactive policies from eligibility checks

table leave_requests | fields: id, employee_id, leave_policy_id, start_date, end_date, reason, status, approved_by, approved_at, rejected_by, rejected_at, rejection_reason, cancelled_by, cancelled_at, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; leave_policy_id -> leave_policies.id; approved_by -> employees.id; rejected_by -> employees.id; cancelled_by -> employees.id | indexes: employee_id: list all leave requests for a given employee (self-service dashboard); status: filter requests by status for manager approval queues and HR reports; leave_policy_id: filter by leave type/policy for reporting; start_date: range queries for calendar views and overlapping-leave detection; end_date: range queries for calendar views and overlapping-leave detection; approved_by: lookup requests approved by a specific manager

table leave_balances | fields: id, employee_id, leave_policy_id, total_entitlement, used_days, remaining_days, fiscal_year, status, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; leave_policy_id -> leave_policies.id | indexes: employee_id: lookup balance for a specific employee (self-service dashboard, balance check before approval); leave_policy_id: filter balances by policy type; fiscal_year: filter balances by fiscal year for accrual and reset operations; employee_id, leave_policy_id, fiscal_year: unique constraint to prevent duplicate balance records per employee-policy-year

table audit_logs | fields: id, entity_type, entity_id, action, old_values, new_values, performed_by, performed_at, ip_address, user_agent, created_at | pk: id | fks: performed_by -> employees.id | indexes: entity_type, entity_id: lookup audit trail for a specific entity (e.g., all changes to a leave request); performed_by: filter audit records by actor for compliance reports; performed_at: time-range queries for audit reports; action: filter by action type (APPROVE, REJECT, CREATE, etc.)

table notifications | fields: id, recipient_id, type, title, message, related_entity_type, related_entity_id, status, created_at, read_at | pk: id | fks: recipient_id -> employees.id | indexes: recipient_id: list notifications for a specific user; status: filter by delivery/read status for notification center; related_entity_type, related_entity_id: lookup notifications tied to a specific leave request or other entity; created_at: chronological ordering for notification feeds
